To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Salmonella enterica Type Three Secretion Systems (T3SSs) are dispensable for invasion into 3-D models and in vivo-like models of human intestinal cells, and (2) T3SSs, including the SPI-1 TSS, are required for Salmonella intracellular replication within 3D models and in vivo.
Salmonella T3SSs do not mediate bacterial invasion into human intestinal cells but are required for bacterial replication within these cells.

Salmonella enterica type three secretory (T3S) system mutants invade and replicate within a 3-D human intestinal model, but the SPI-1 TSS is dispensable for Salmonellae to penetrate the epithelial cell layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of bacterial pathogenesis in the gastrointestinal tract.
elucidating mechanisms that underlie the pathogenicity of Salmonella enterica.
the development of a 3-D model of human intestinal cells and its application to the study of Salmonella pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Salmonella enteropathogenicity in the gastrointestinal tract is independent of T3SSs, as the T3SS is not required for invasion or colonization of the 3-D model of intestinal epithelium, and that the 3-D organoid is a useful model of human enteric disease, which can be utilized to study other enteropathogens.
the T3SSs of Salmonella enterica are dispensable for invasion of 3-D human intestinal epithelial models but are required for replication within these cells.
T3SS are required for intracelluar growth of Salmonella in 3-D intestinal epithelium, but are not required for invasion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T3SS are dispensable for invasion of Salmonella into 3-D human intestinal epithelial models, and that T3SS is required for intracellular replication of Salmonella in these models.
T3SS mutants are not defective for invasion, but are defective for intracellular growth, which is a more important phenotype in the context of pathogenesis.
the Salmonella SPI1 T3SS is not required to invade into 3D intestinal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3-D model of the intestinal epithelium is a more accurate model to study the interactions of Salmonella with the human intestinal epitheliam compared to monolayers.
the SPI-1 TSS is dispensable for invasion into differentiated 3-D intestinal epithelial cells and that SPI-1, SPI-2, and SPI-5 are all required for intracellular growth.

the 3D intestinal model we used is a more accurate representation of the in vivo infection model, and that it can be used to study the role of Salmonella type III secretion system (T3SS) in enteric infections.
